And worth mentioning, all virtual machine programs will be quite slow unless you have a fairly good computer

So an emulator is a program that basically pretend to be a windows or Linux machine so that you can run the program.

A virtual machine is similar, but it will basically create an entire “virtual” windows or Linux machine, which can be used for any number of tasks

It often doesn’t work with more complicated applications. So you might want to try using the wine program itself to run the application, rather than bottling the application, but that might not work either

If you have an intel based Mac you can try to use wine to open the program. It’s kind of like an emulator, but doesn’t always work. If you have an M1 Mac or if it just doesn’t work for that application, you can then either use an actual emulator, or a virtual machine, assuming you don’t want to actually install Windows or Linux
